sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. sample of marked blind two-replicate observations \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i,S_{i1},S_{i2})\).
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units have finite-stratum \(X_i\), compact latent dose \(A_i\), and bounded potential-outcome schedules generated simultaneously as \(Y_i(a)=h(a,X_i,V_i)\) by a jointly measurable response surface, with \(V_i\perp A_i\mid X_i\); the stratum-specific causal means are continuous on \(I\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\), with independent errors that need not be identically distributed or symmetric and may have spectral gaps; only \(E[U_2]=0\) fixes location.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: At deterministic \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), use relaxed outer order-\(d\) B-spline families for \(f_x,q_x\), finite atomic characteristic-function families for \(\phi_1,\phi_2\), and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\). The outer splines allow the exact Jackson approximation errors in positivity, normalization, and domination; they are feasibility devices rather than asserted model laws. Profile the clipped ADRF extrema with deterministic tie-breaking and the stated empty-set rule.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Our contributions include establishing identifiability without any assumption on the noise except for coordinate independence.
We identify the average dose-response function for a continuously valued error contaminated treatment by a weighted conditional expectation.
Uniform confidence bands in deconvolution with unknown error distribution.

body.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates. Analytic cocycle identification and an explicit structural response-surface condition establish the causal identifying functional. The empirical-characteristic-function construction is repaired as a relaxed outer-sieve inversion and yields a uniformly honest simultaneous band with finite clipped endpoints and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\). Its empirical-grid constraints do not prove a shrinking inverse diameter, so no \(r_n\) upper rate is claimed. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus also remains unresolved, and there is no matched honest-band rate.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not provide a shrinking uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band for blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with open spectral zero sets. In particular, the present empirical-grid outer set lacks a quantitative marked inverse modulus, and the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus needed for a sharp all-band converse remains unproved.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem: compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, near-origin conditioning supports qualitative cocycle inversion, and the causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element and continuity of the stratum-specific causal mean bridge that observed regression quotient to the point-dose causal curve. The distinction between qualitative identification and quantitative confidence-set diameter is essential here.
project_justification.fill: The paper now delivers an explicit conservative inference map: deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic dimensions; simultaneous probability-, marked-, and mass-channel radii; relaxed compact outer signal sieves that contain unconstrained Jackson approximants; a joint feasible set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. It proves uniform simultaneous coverage and the universal bound \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\). A shrinking-width theorem would require a redesigned protected-cube analytic-polynomial contrast and a marked signed-channel analogue; the current construction does not establish \(O(r_n)\).

body.related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle, constrained polynomial estimator, and compact-support \(L^2\) minimax experiment that inform the analytic machinery; their qualitative identification theorem requires neither the fixed \(q_e\)-moment radius nor the uniform pair \((\nu_0,c_0)\), which are paper-specific quantitative restrictions here. Their rate argument uses a protected-region integrated contrast with nearly parametric forward error and does not supply a Lipschitz inverse for the present grid set whose tolerance already contains polynomial Jackson error. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki (2018) develop deconvolution bands with an unknown error distribution using an auxiliary error sample, together with a symmetric-error repeated-measurement route; that design differs from two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates and has neither the marked quotient nor joint cell-mass profiling. Kato and Sasaki (2019) obtain multiplier-bootstrap uniform bands under conventional spectral conditions. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski restrictions to retain coverage without completeness, but do not establish a shrinking marked-quotient band here. Babii studies honest expected diameter for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies a testing-to-expected-length reduction only after a marked modulus is established. None of these sources proves the missing quantitative diameter for the current empirical-grid outer set.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The causal bridge, analytic-cocycle identification, simultaneous transform concentration, relaxed outer-sieve embedding, and clipped uniform coverage are proved. The current grid feasibility set nevertheless has no quantitative inverse modulus: its forward tolerance contains polynomial Jackson error, analytic continuation amplifies that tolerance, and the grid restrictions do not reproduce the source's protected-cube integrated contrast. Accordingly, the proved upper result has only \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), not shrinking expected width. The sharp-rate program requires a redesigned analytic-polynomial confidence construction for both the probability and signed marked channels. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli outcome modulus remains the separate lower-side obstruction.
body.honest_scope: The model retains the fixed quantitative restrictions on compact dose support, bounded outcomes, Sobolev radii, overlap, error moments, local spectral modulus, finite-stratum masses, and the structural causal response surface. The explicit relaxed outer-sieve band is uniformly honest for all sufficiently large \(n\) and is universally clipped to width at most \(2B_Y\). No \(o(1)\), \(O(r_n)\), minimax-matching, or off-event analytic-stability claim is made. Establishing a shrinking band requires a different protected-cube contrast construction; establishing a matching converse also requires the unresolved fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus. The present theorem therefore certifies conservative simultaneous coverage, not the advertised optimal rate.
body.interpretation: The observed two-channel law identifies the continuous regression curve \(q_x/f_x\). Structural exogeneity first equates this curve with the stratum-specific causal mean almost everywhere in dose; positivity and continuity then extend the equality to every target dose. Coordinatewise weak unconfoundedness and almost-sure consistency alone would not suffice because they permit treatment-dependent diagonal modifications on null sets.
